text:
Noah: Hey folks, opened my first PR touching runtime/api_adapter and a small config for model pinning. Branch: feat/noah/pin-model-v2. Quick q: is the team prefix (runtime/) required? Also hitting a failing pre-commit hook for types.

Priya: Congrats! We don't require the team prefix but it's encouraged for cross-team visibility: feat/runtime/noah/pin-model-v2 would be fine. Keep branch names <= 72 chars after your name.

Alex: For reviewers, CODEOWNERS will auto-request @eng-runtime and @platform when you touch runtime/*, but add specific people in the PR body if you want faster eyeballs. We prefer two approvals for runtime changes: one runtime eng and one infra/platform.

Noah: Thanks. The pre-commit error says my mypy failure is in a generated protobuf file. I didn't touch it. Any guidance?

Priya: If it's generated, add a # type: ignore at the import or regenerate the protos with the same toolchain. Usually run `make protos` or `scripts/gen_protos.sh`. If CI regenerates them, rebase and re-run `make proto-check` locally.

ci-bot: CI queued for feat/noah/pin-model-v2  build 4788  status: pending

Noah: I ran `make protos` and that fixed my local mypy, re-ran pre-commit and all hooks passed. Pushed. CI started but one integration test timed out (integration/latency-test).

Rosa: Integration timeouts can be flakes. Label the PR `test/flaky` and re-run the failing job from Circle. If it fails repeatedly, add `test/investigate` and ping @Rosa. We have a flaky-tests board where we track failures.

Alex: Merge strategy: squash-merge for small feature flags and chore changes. For iterative runtime features that preserve history, do merge commit and add a short changelog entry. Also add an entry to the release notes draft if this affects behavior.

Noah: Good to know. One more: commit message template? I used: "feat(runtime): pin model v2 for better determinism". Should I add an issue ref?

Priya: That's fine. If there's a ticket, add "Fixes #<issue>" in the body. Otherwise the Conventional Commits subject is enough. Also add a short test plan in the PR body: how you tested locally and what to watch for after rollout.

Noah: All green now and requested reviewers. Thanks for the quick orientation, appreciate the help :wave:

Alex: Welcome aboard Noah! If you're unsure about labels, ping #devex and someone will help triage. Also here's a short checklist you can paste into PR body: 1) run pre-commit 2) run unit + integration subset 3) add reviewers 4) add labels (area/runtime, test/flake if needed).

Noah: Saved the checklist, thanks :thumbsup:
